'''Gopi K. Podila''' (September 14, 1957<ref>According to Zabasearch</ref> – February 12, 2010) was an [[Indian Americans|Indian American]] biologist who served as a professor at the [[University of Alabama in Huntsville]]. He was one of three faculty members killed in [[2010 University of Alabama in Huntsville shooting|a mass shooting]] at the university on February 12, 2010.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/us/Indian-American-professor-among-3-killed-in-US-university-shooting/articleshow/5568190.cms|title=Indian-American professor among 3 killed in US university shooting |date=February 13, 2010|work=Times of India|accessdate=February 13, 2010}}</ref> Podila was chairperson of the university's department of biological sciences, with a particular interest in the ecology of ''[[Populus]]'' and their [[mycorrhiza]]l symbionts.

==Research career==
He listed his research interests as "engineering tree biomass for bioenergy, functional genomics of plant-microbe interactions, plant molecular biology and biotechnology".
<ref>{{cite web
| url         =http://www.uah.edu/biology/podila.html
| title       =Dr. G. K. Podila, Chair, Department of Biological Sciences
| publisher   = University of Alabama in Huntsville
| archiveurl  =https://web.archive.org/web/20080613212317/http://www.uah.edu/biology/podila.html
| archivedate =2008-06-13
}}</ref>

In particular, Podila studied genes that regulate growth in fast growing trees, especially poplar and aspen. He advocated prospective use of fast growing trees and grasses as an [[Cellulosic ethanol|alternative]] to [[Corn ethanol|corn]] sources for producing [[Ethanol fuel|ethanol]].<ref>[http://www.energy-daily.com/reports/Trees_And_Grass_May_Be_Able_To_Produce_Ethanol_Without_Poisoning_The_Oceans_999.html Trees And Grass May Be Able To Produce Ethanol Without Poisoning The Oceans.] Energy Daily, January 22, 2008. Retrieved February 13, 2010.</ref> He was also the coordinator of an international consortium of institutions that has deciphered the [[genome]] of [[mycorrhiza|mycorrhizal fungus]], a fungus whose [[symbiosis|symbiotic]] properties allow trees to generate large amounts of biomass.<ref>[http://news.softpedia.com/news/The-Genome-of-an-Important-Symbiotic-Fungus-Has-Been-Sequenced-32411.shtml The Genome of an Important Symbiotic Fungus Has Been Sequenced. The first mycorrhizal fungal genome project was a success.] [[Softpedia]], August 9, 2006. Retrieved February 13, 2006.</ref>

G. K. Podila received a B.Sc. degree from [[Acharya Nagarjuna University|Nagarjuna University]] in India.<ref name="h"/> He obtained a master's degree from [[Louisiana State University]] in 1983 and a PhD in molecular biology from [[Indiana State University]] in 1987.<ref name="h">[https://books.google.com/books?id=uAheSu_8hKsC&dq=%22Gopi+K.+Podila%22&pg=PP10 Handbook of molecular and cellular methods in biology and medicine.] [[Taylor and Francis]], 2002. {{ISBN|0-8493-0815-1}}</ref> Prior to joining the [[University of Alabama in Huntsville]], he worked at [[Michigan Technological University]] from 1990 to 2002.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.pravasiherald.com/index.php/comments/in_memory_of_dr._gopi_krishna_podila/ |title=Pravasi Herald |publisher=Pravasi Herald |date=2010-02-17 |accessdate=2010-04-07 }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Podila was an Editorial Board member of the journals ''Symbiosis'',<ref>[http://www.symbiosisjournal.com/Editorial_Board.shtml Editorial Board] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090829221327/http://www.symbiosisjournal.com/Editorial_Board.shtml |date=2009-08-29 }}, ''Symbiosis''. Retrieved February 13, 2010.</ref> ''[[New Phytologist]]'',<ref>[http://www.newphytologist.com/view/0/editorialBoard.html Editorial Board] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090703083330/http://www.newphytologist.com/view/0/editorialBoard.html |date=2009-07-03 }}, ''New Phytologist''. Retrieved February 13, 2010.</ref> ''Physiology and Molecular Biology of Plants'',<ref>[https://www.springer.com/life+sciences/plant+sciences/journal/12298?detailsPage=editorialBoard Editorial Board], ''Physiology and Molecular Biology of Plants'', [[Springer-Verlag]]. Retrieved February 13, 2010.</ref>  and ''Journal of Plant Interactions''.<ref>[http://www.tandf.co.uk/journals/journal.asp?issn=1742-9145&linktype=5 Editorial Board],  ''Journal of Plant Interactions''. Retrieved February 13, 2010.</ref><ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.deepdyve.com/lp/springer-journals/obituary-D6WP6vwiPZ | title=Obituary: Dr. G. K. Podila |publisher= [[DeepDyve]] | journal=Symbiosis |date=March 1, 2010 | volume=50 | pages=117–118 | doi=10.1007/s13199-010-0061-7 |accessdate=10 Dec 2015| doi-access=free }}</ref>

At the time of his death Podila was a Councilor of the International Symbiosis Society.<ref>[http://people.bu.edu/iss/aboutiss.htm About ISS.] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091009032343/http://people.bu.edu/iss/aboutiss.htm |date=2009-10-09 }} International Symbiosis Society. Retrieved February 13, 2010.</ref> He is survived by his widow, Vani Podila, and two daughters.

==UAH shooting==
{{main|2010 University of Alabama in Huntsville shooting}}
On February 12, 2010, Amy Bishop, a faculty member in Podila's department, drew a handgun during a staff meeting and shot six people. Podila and two other faculty members were killed. Bishop was taken into custody outside the building and charged with capital murder. Bishop was convicted and sentenced to life in prison.<ref name="Nature">{{cite journal| last =Anonymous | title =Survivors of the 2010 University of Alabama shooting chose not to push for the death penalty.| journal =Nature| volume =490| issue =7418| doi =10.1038/490006a| year = 2012| page =6| pmid =23050272| doi-access =free}}</ref>
